[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Chaos Engineering and Resilience Testing in Performance Engineering"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Traditional performance testing focuses on measuring system throughput and latency under anticipated loads. However, modern distributed systems frequently fail in unpredictable ways due to network partitions, hardware degradation, and upstream service outages. Chaos Engineering is the discipline of experimenting on a system in production to build confidence in the system's capability to withstand turbulent conditions."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Principles of Chaos Engineering"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Start by defining steady state. Measure a measurable output of a system that indicates normal behavior, such as successful requests per second."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Hypothesize that steady state will continue in both the control group and the experimental group."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Introduce variables that mimic real-world events, such as server crashes, network latency, or database failures."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Try to disprove the hypothesis by looking for a difference in steady state between the control and experimental groups."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Designing a Chaos Experiment"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"When integrating chaos experiments into your performance testing pipeline, you must establish a blast radius to minimize user impact. Below is an example configuration using the LitmusChaos framework to inject network latency into a target microservice during a load test."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: litmuschaos.io/v1alpha1
kind: ChaosEngine
metadata:
  name: engine-nginx
  namespace: default
spec:
  engineState: 'active'
  annotationCheck: 'false'
  appinfo:
    appns: 'default'
    applabel: 'app=nginx'
    appkind: 'deployment'
  chaosServiceAccount: litmus-admin
  experiments:
    - name: pod-network-latency
      spec:
        components:
          env:
            - name: TOTAL_CHAOS_DURATION
              value: '60'
            - name: NETWORK_LATENCY
              value: '2000'"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Analyzing Resilience Metrics"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"During chaos injection, monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) closely. Look for metrics such as Time to Detect (TTD) and Time to Recover (TTR). A resilient system will gracefully degrade performance rather than cascading into a total outage."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Error Rate Spikes: Ensure fallback mechanisms catch failures and return cached responses."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Circuit Breakers: Verify that circuit breakers trip correctly to protect downstream dependencies."},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"By proactively introducing failure during controlled performance runs, teams can uncover hidden failure modes and improve overall software resilience before issues affect real users."}]
